Medium Affected: OTHER

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 30.069168, -83.525566 (Approximated from establishment)
Report DescriptionCALLER IS REPORTING THAT A PULP AND PAPER COMPANY HAS A SYSTEM EXTRACTING METHANOL AND HYDROGEN SULFIDE AND ATTEMPTING TO BURN IT. BUT THEY ARE CREATING MORE METHANOL THAN THEY ARE PERMITTED TO BURN. THEY ARE TAKING 55 GALLON DRUMS OF METHANOL AND HAND PUMPING IT INTO THE BOILERS WITH OUT REPORTING AND METERING HOW MUCH THEY ARE BURNING. THEY DIVERT METHANOL TO THE WASTE WATER TANK TRYING TO DELATE THE METHANOL AND OVER FLOWING THE WASTE WATER TANK AND MAKING 6 EMPLOYEES SICK ENOUGH TO NEED TO GO TO THE EMERGENCY ROOM. THEY REBOIL THE WASTE WATER AND THE METHANOL AND IT EVAPORATES INTO THE PLANT. METHANOL IS ALSO BEING SENT TO THE WASTE WATER TREATMENT PLANT. EMPLOYEES ARE EXPOSED TO AIRBORNE METHANOL

ORIGINAL REPORT READS: THE CALLER STATED THAT A FREIGHT TRAIN HAD (20) CARS AND (1) LOCOMOTIVE THAT DERAILED AFTER STRIKING A TRACTOR TRAILER TRUCK AT A GRADE CROSSING. BECAUSE OF THIS INCIDENT THE CONDUCTOR IS COMPLAINING OF BRUISED RIBS AND THE DRIVER OF THE TRUCK SUSTAINED UNSPECIFIED INJURIES. BOTH PARTIES WERE TRANSPORTED TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL FOR TREATMENT. THE CALLER ALSO STATED THAT THE ENGINEER WAS SENT TO THE HOSPITAL, HOWEVER IT WAS MORE OF A PRECAUTIONARY MEASURE. BECAUSE OF THIS INCIDENTS HIGHWAY 7 AND THE MAIN LINE TRACK WERE CLOSED IN ALL DIRECTIONS. ACCORDING TO THE CALLER (19) OF THE TWENTY CARS THAT DERAILED WERE EMPTY, HOWEVER THE 20TH CAR WAS LOADED WITH RAILWAY EQUIPMENT. CURRENTLY IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE TRACTOR TRAILER RELEASED ANY MATERIAL DURING THIS INCIDENT. THERE WERE DAMAGES, HOWEVER THE PRICE POINT FOR THOSE DAMAGES IS STILL UNKNOWN TO THE CALLER.

ON JANUARY 5TH DURING ROUTINE STATION CHECK, THE SENIOR OPERATOR NOTICED STAINED GRAVEL BETWEEN SUCTION VALVE AND INJECTION VALVES. A WORK CREW WAS CALLED TO INVESTIGATE AND DIG TEST HOLES AROUND APPURTENANCES ASSOCIATED WITH THE PIPELINE TO INVESTIGATE WHETHER OR NOT THE STAINING WAS ASSOCIATED WITH A LEAK. AFTER DIGGING AN INITIAL TEST HOLE TO A DEPTH OF ABOUT 2 TO 3 FT., GROUND WATER BEGAN FILLING THE HOLE AND A SMALL AMOUNT OF BLACK LOOKING OIL BEGAN TO EXUDE INTO THE TEST HOLE. UPON FINDING PRODUCT, THE LOOP WAS ISOLATED FROM THE MAIN LINE BY CLOSING OFF SUCTION AND DISCHARGE VALVES. SORBENT MATERIALS WERE USED TO REMOVE OIL FROM THE WATER SURFACE IN THE TEST HOLE. THE ADDITIONAL TEST HOLES ALSO FILLED WITH GROUND WATER AND SEVERAL EXUDED OIL ON TO THE GROUND WATER SURFACE. OIL WAS ALSO OBSERVED IN THE OIL/WATER SEPARATOR (OWS). TO ENSURE THAT OIL WOULD NOT REACH THE OWS DISCHARGE POINT AT THE POND, THE OWS DISCHARGE VALVE WAS CLOSED AND DISCHARGE WAS ONLY ALLOWED DIRECTLY INTO THE SUMP. MONITORING OF THE OWS AND PRODUCT RECOVERY WAS INITIATED ON A DAILY BASIS.
